olivia: Heads-up — reproducing a slow, sustained KV cache memory climb on Dedicated when clients stream very long contexts (~25k-50k tokens). Hosted runs the same workload without growth. Private on-prem shows larger fragmentation and more frequent page evicts. Repro steps and quick logs below.

sam: Can you paste the minimal repro and the allocator stats?

olivia: repro: run loadtest with `--streaming --max-tokens 50000 --batch 1` against dedicated pool A. Observed steady +0.8MB/s per active connection. Attached sample jemalloc and /proc/pid/pagemap dumps:

olivia: ```
jemalloc: allocated: 3.1G active: 2.9G mapped: 4.2G
kvcache: resident=2.1G anon=1.2G page_faults=120k
evict_count=47 last_evict=2026-05-11T14:22:01Z
```

kai: Did you compare kernel pinned pages / hugetlb usage? On-prem GPUs have different hugepage alignment which can fragment KV frames.

maria: Also check batching heuristics — Dedicated had an autoscaler change last week that changed max_batch_size from 32->48; could increase KV churn.

olivia: Good call. I profiled kernel selection traces: hosted uses optimized kernel tree K-3 for long seqs, dedicated fell back to K-1 after a quantized-kernel regression; that altered per-step memory pattern. Snippet:

olivia: ```
[profile] kernel_select: model=redwood-3-large seq=4096 -> K-3
[profile] kernel_select: model=redwood-3-large seq=4096 -> K-1 (dedicated)
```

sam: If dedicated falls back to K-1, KV frames might be larger per token. Can you share per-token kv size delta?

olivia: Per-token delta ~ +32 bytes/frame when K-1 used. Over 50k tokens -> ~1.6MB per request, 500 concurrent -> big.

kai: VPC MTU might exacerbate evict latencies if page reclaim stalls IO. Any network-level drops on Private?

olivia: On-prem had occasional `dmesg` logs: `kworker: page_cache_reclaim blocked for 200ms`; plus Numa node interleaving. Fragmentation % from `/proc/buddyinfo` higher on-prem.

maria: Let's try two experiments: 1) force K-3 on Dedicated to see if growth stops, 2) revert recent autoscaler batch-size change. I'll open a canary.

deploy-bot: deployment roller started by maria for team/serving-runtime - canary on dedicated-pool-A (revision ab12cd) at 2061234580

sam: Also capture kvslot aging histogram (helpful to see reclaim vs evict rates). If reuse window too long, we'll accumulate stale frames.

olivia: Attached quick histogram (abbrev): `age_buckets: [0-1s: 12k, 1-10s: 2k, 10-100s: 900, >100s: 420]` — tail looks heavy on Dedicated.

kai: If kernel selection change increased per-frame size and batching increased concurrency, reuse hit-rate can drop. Could combine a batching cap patch + KV throttle.

maria: I pushed a temp config: `max_batch_size=32`, `kv_reclaim_threshold=0.65` to canary. Will report in 10m.

olivia: Thanks — will run long-context replay against canary and post results.

sam: Also please add `--jemalloc.stats true` to the repro run and upload `/proc/vmstat` snapshot.

olivia: Will do. If canary looks good, we should add an integration test that replays long streaming contexts across envs and check `mapped` growth < 100MB/10min.

kai: +1 for automated regression. tagging @security for on-prem kernel tweaks.

maria: FYI, there's a known quirk on older on-prem nvidia driver that affects page pinning; ops already have a patch we can try.

olivia: Great. I'll collate logs and update thread. :thumbsup:
